2. Systemic amitriptyline (tricyclic) toxicity from transdermal absorption (anticholinergic/CNS effects contributing to delirium).
3. Lidocaine systemic toxicity from transdermal absorption (contributing to CNS depression/ataxia; potential cardiac toxicity).
4. Mixed/combined topical anesthetic toxicity (synergistic CNS depression and delirium from combined ketamine + amitriptyline + lidocaine absorption).
5. Multifactorial acute delirium (age, Parkinson disease, polypharmacy, metabolic/infectious causes) or less likely acute cerebrovascular event (cerebellar/brainstem stroke) — considered because of altered mental status and focal‑mimicking features but lower probability given nonfocal exam and positive toxicology.
